'''Karen I. Aardal''' (born 1961){{r|born}} is a Norwegian and Dutch applied mathematician, theoretical computer scientist, and [[operations research]]er. Her research involves [[combinatorial optimization]], [[integer programming]], [[approximation algorithm]]s, and [[Optimal facility location|facility location]], with applications such as positioning emergency vehicles to optimize their response time.{{r|slwm}} She is a professor in the Delft Institute of Applied Mathematics at the [[Delft University of Technology]],{{r|prof}} and the chair of the [[Mathematical Optimization Society]] for the 2016–2019 term.{{r|mos|app}}

==Education and career==
Aardal is originally from Norway.{{r|slwm}} She earned her Ph.D. in 1992 at the [[Université catholique de Louvain]] in Belgium. Her dissertation, ''On the Solution of One and Two-Level Capacitated Facility Location Problems by the Cutting Plane Approach'', was supervised by [[Laurence Wolsey]].{{r|mg}} Her dissertation won the second-place SOLA Dissertation Award of the [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]] Section on Location Analysis.{{r|sola}}

Aardal was formerly a researcher at the Dutch [[Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica]], and additionally affiliated with [[Eindhoven University of Technology]] since 2005. She moved to Delft in 2008.{{r|naar}}

She was elected to the 2019 class of [[Fellow]]s of the [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.informs.org/Recognizing-Excellence/Fellows/Fellows-Alphabetical-List|title=Fellows: Alphabetical List|publisher=[[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]]|accessdate=2019-10-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510220119/https://www.informs.org/Recognizing-Excellence/Fellows/Fellows-Alphabetical-List|archive-date=2019-05-10|url-status=dead}}</ref>
